story: From 1973 to 1990, General Augusto Pinochet ruled Chile after a coup, and thousands were killed or disappeared. Since democracy returned, the country has been run by centre-left and centre-right governments that kept Pinochet's legacy at arm's length. In 2026 Chile inaugurated José Antonio Kast, who campaigned for Pinochet as a young man, its most right-wing leader since the return of democracy (AP via WTOP).

Kast took office on 11 March, replacing the leftist Gabriel Boric, and signed half a dozen emergency decrees on border security and deportations before his first speech. Chile's foreign population doubled between 2017 and 2024, mostly Venezuelans fleeing collapse, and Kast linked them to rising crime, though Chile remains one of the region's safest countries, with a homicide rate of 5.4 per 100,000 (Teleamazonas/AFP). Five days in, he stood among excavators at the Peruvian border to launch a "Border Shield" of trenches and barriers across the Atacama Desert, and sent bills to Congress to make illegal entry a crime and cut migrants' social benefits (NPR via WRVO). He has threatened about 336,000 undocumented migrants with expulsion. Investors welcomed his promise of $6 billion in spending cuts over 18 months, though economists doubt it can be done without hitting social benefits. Two of his ministers once defended Pinochet-era generals in court.
briefing.power: A presidential republic. The president is directly elected for a single four-year term with no immediate re-election; Congress has a Chamber of Deputies and Senate. Two attempts to replace the Pinochet-era constitution failed in referendums in 2022 and 2023.
briefing.holders: President José Antonio Kast (Republican Party), since March 2026.
